name: Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasm Associated with PDGFRA Rearrangement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2022)

criteria.description: Presence of PDGFRA gene rearrangement confirmed by molecular genetic testing (e.g., FISH, RT-PCR, or NGS)
Peripheral blood eosinophilia >1.5 x 10^9/L or tissue eosinophilic infiltration
Evidence of myeloid or lymphoid neoplasm with features consistent with clonal proliferation
Exclusion of other causes of eosinophilia such as parasitic infection or allergic disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Detection of PDGFRA rearrangement with associated eosinophilia and evidence of myeloid or lymphoid neoplasm
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires molecular confirmation of PDGFRA rearrangement; clinical and hematologic features support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Sustained eosinophilia is a hallmark feature

searchTerms: enlarged spleen from blood cell production
spleen swelling due to extra blood cell formation
spleen enlargement caused by blood cell growth outside marrow

pathognomonic.symptomName: PDGFRA gene fusion detected by molecular testing

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms including weight loss and night sweats
searchTerms: weight loss with fever and night sweating
general symptoms like fatigue and sweating at night
unexplained weight loss and night sweats

common.notes: Due to marrow involvement or hemolysis
searchTerms: low red cells with pale complexion

common.symptomName: Cutaneous manifestations such as urticaria or rash
common.notes: May be related to eosinophilic infiltration

common.symptomName: Dyspnea due to pulmonary eosinophilic infiltration
searchTerms: shortness of breath due to lung inflammation

occasional.notes: Due to eosinophilic infiltration or paraneoplastic effects

occasional.symptomName: Gastrointestinal symptoms such as abdominal pain or diarrhea

occasional.notes: May be present in lymphoid involvement

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain due to marrow expansion

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement with seizures or cognitive impairment
searchTerms: brain symptoms like confusion or seizures

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to eosinophilic infiltration
rare.notes: May present as proteinuria or renal failure
Rare eosinophilic infiltration of ocular tissues

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric symptoms such as depression or anxiety
searchTerms: psychiatric problems like sadness or worry

laboratory: Elevated serum tryptase in some cases
imaging: Splenomegaly and hepatomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT
other: Bone marrow biopsy showing eosinophilic infiltration and myeloid proliferation
Immunophenotyping to exclude other hematologic malignancies

distinguishingFeatures: Variable eosinophilia without specific gene fusion
Different response to tyrosine kinase inhibitors
Eosinophilia with organ damage but no neoplastic proliferation

redFlags: Severe unexplained eosinophilia with organ infiltration
Failure to respond to corticosteroids or conventional therapy
references: Arber DA, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 5th Edition, 2022.
Gotlib J. World Health Organization-defined eosinophilic disorders: 2017 update on diagnosis, risk stratification, and management. Am J Hematol. 2017.
Cools J, et al. A tyrosine kinase created by fusion of the PDGFRA and FIP1L1 genes as a therapeutic target of imatinib in idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2003.
